answers.text: Tell it: always give exactly three lines from the driver's message, in this order - drop-off time, pallet count, any damage noted - nothing added on top.
Have it list the calls out and give me the number that still need a follow-up at the end.
The finish time seems off given when they're starting - I'd expect that to be sorted well before the next day, not still running on the 23rd.
The increase in invoices doesn't check out - 96 to 118 is closer to 23%, not the 20% stated. I'd leave the balance figures for someone else to look at properly.
I'd sign off the second output, it gives the actual numbers - 827 of 940 - so the 88% can be checked. The first one could still be right, but you'd have to rerun it to know for sure.

The second email is the one I'd send, since it has the real volume figures behind the ask. The first one isn't necessarily wrong, it just doesn't give the supplier anything to check, so it's not ready to send as it is.
1. No, I'd hold the pricing back for now. 2. Yes, fine as it is. 3. No, that draft isn't signed off. 4. No, wouldn't risk it even though it's on their site. 5. No, that's someone's home address.
I'd take out the hourly rates and the retainer cap before pasting it in, and go carefully with the non-disclosure part too since it names both companies directly.
Before the reconciliation goes out each month I check the closing totals against the warehouse system - a quick cross-check, nothing more elaborate than that.
I still think the extraction step is the risky one - if it misreads the invoice, that carries through the rest of the process.
